pr_title: fix(chromium): close all javascript dialogs when closing context

issue_context.title: [BUG] context.close() doesn't close stray onbeforeunload dialog in chromium
issue_context.body:
**Context:** - Playwright Version: 1.17.2 - Operating System: Mac - Python version: Python 3.9.10 - Browser: All **Code Snippet** ```python from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright import pytest HEADLESS = True HEADLESS = False WAIT = 5000 @pytest.fixture(scope='session', params=('firefox', 'chromium', 'webkit')) def browser_vendor(request): yield request.param @pytest.fixture(scope='session') def browser(browser_vendor): with sync_playwright() as playwright: browser = getattr(playwright, browser_vendor) instance = browser.launch(headless=HEADLESS) yield instance instance.close() @pytest.fixture def context(browser): context = browser.new_context() yield context context.close() @pytest.fixture def page(context): page = context.new_page() page.set_default_timeout(WAIT) yield page page.close() html = '''
div_text
''' ask_to_leave_script = ''' // interestingly Firefox webdriver doesn't show thes dialogs at all, even though this code works in normal Firefox window.addEventListener('beforeunload', function (e) { // Cancel the event e.preventDefault(); // mozilla will now always show dialog // Chrome requires returnValue to be set e.returnValue = 'Fnord'; }); ''' def test_before_unload(page): # delay unload page.set_content(html) page.evaluate(ask_to_leave_script) # page needs a change otherwise the onbeforeunload doesn't trigger page.fill('text=input_label', value='fnord') page.click("body") with page.expect_event("dialog") as dialog_info: page.close(run_before_unload=True) dialog = dialog_info.value assert dialog.type == "beforeunload" # with page.expect_event("close"): # dialog.accept() context = page.context context.close() # browser = context.browser # browser.close() ``` **Describe the bug** When dealing with stray leftover dialogs in (often background windows) Chromium doesn't behave the same as the other browsers, in that it hangs forever in `context.close()` while Safari and FF close the context just fine. It is my understanding that context.close() is what should give test isolation and is what should happen between tests. In any case, the three browsers should behave the same way. The workaround of course, is to just close the dialog programmatically. But this is still annoying.
comments: Seems to be a dupe of https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/issues/10476

review_comments: Let's comment that headed chrome does not close with beforeunload open, but not with any other dialog types, and we do not expect any new beforeunload dialogs because our close does not trigger them.
